core_conclusion: neuroGravity is a physics-informed deep learning model that embeds the gravity law inside a neural architecture to reconstruct full urban mobility networks from partial flow observations plus only public facility and population distributions, and to transfer to cities with no survey data. Its learned regional embeddings correlate strongly with socioeconomic and livability status, serving as scalable proxies for costly travel surveys. Spatial income segregation is identified as the key determinant of transferability: reconstruction is most reliable when source and target cities share similar segregation levels, and a purpose-built segregation index predicts transfer performance in advance. Mobility flow proxies for over 1,200 cities worldwide are released.
why_it_matters: Attacks the core data gap in urban science by producing credible OD flow networks from open facility and population layers alone, making mobility modeling feasible in resource-limited and undeveloped regions. It converts transferability from an untested hope into a measurable, predictable property via a segregation-similarity index, turns a flow model into a socioeconomic sensor through its node embeddings, and ships a global public good of 1,200+ city mobility networks with open code.
why_nature: Fits Nature Computational Science exactly: a new computational model, a discovered scientific regularity (spatial income segregation governs cross-city transferability), and a released global dataset in one package. It extends the physics-informed machine learning paradigm from physical to social systems, carries strong Global-South equity relevance, and is unusually honest about when transfer fails by supplying a diagnostic index rather than a blanket performance claim. Open code, Source Data for Figs. 3-5 and an extensive Supplementary meet the journal's reproducibility bar.
added_value_to_my_research: Segregation-style domain-shift index -> pre-deployment go/no-go diagnostic for transferring accessibility and telehealth models across regions
Satellite/building-function substitution for OSM facilities -> honest error budget for 2SFCA supply layers in under-mapped regions
Segregation-conditioned or invariant training -> one accessibility model with an interpretable social-context knob instead of per-region refits
Symbolic distillation of the learned deterrence function -> empirically grounded, regionally varying distance-decay kernels for R2SFCA
Reconstructed OD flows with uncertainty -> flow-weighted primary-care and mental-health accessibility where no travel survey exists
